correctness.rationale: Exact payoff reduction from ideal-point distance advantage and independent cost CDF. Strict within-half convexity for every q>1 reduces all continuous policy deviations to 3 anchors; the anchor best-response table yields necessary and sufficient threshold comparisons. At q=1 the full piecewise-affine payoff on each half identifies all maximizing intervals at e=1/3 and excludes unlisted candidate pairs, completing the infinite policy domain proof. Direct turnout evaluations prove both limits and jump. Independent verification code performed 13,750 exact rational grid equilibrium comparisons and 189 exact finite midpoint convexity checks as supporting evidence only.

originality.rationale: Model-specific full pure-Nash classification and a sharp endogenous turnout jump were not entailed by inspected primary results: Wolf–Meir assumes continuous positive voter density; Kamada–Kojima already studies this exact triad of voter locations but uses a three-element candidate policy set, compulsory probabilistic voting, and winning/refinement payoffs; Bhaskar–Pyne treats discrete voters but not the independent power-cost turnout rule. The zero-turnout collocation exclusion, half-center equilibria, q=1 critical continuum, and turnout discontinuity require the present distinct payoff. Historical priority risk is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: Kamada–Kojima discuss an equivalence of winning probabilities between some compulsory and costly voting models; although this is not an equivalence of the unnormalized vote-share objective here, earlier separate turnout papers may encode the same special case.
Published full Kamada–Kojima journal version was compared through a public 2013 working-paper version; the paper itself, not journal revision metadata, supplies conceptual overlap.
The scientific claim is only for three exact voter masses, not for a continuous positive voter density; no smoothing robustness is inferred.
Semantic published-record retrieval is not proof that an equivalent unpublished or differently indexed result does not exist.

value.rationale: Exact endogenous participation creates a structural change from half-center profiles to fully extreme policies even while a strict majority has ideal point 1/2 (q=2, 1/5<e<1/4). The theorem fully resolves pure Nash outcomes over continuous candidate policies, identifies a nontrivial q=1 continuum at exact balance, and calculates a strictly positive turnout discontinuity. These properties are absent from compulsory probabilistic three-policy outcomes and constitute a motivated sharp benchmark for atomically polarized electorates.
